taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026, 11:59 PM PT.

PT on Oct 30, 2026: US DST ends Nov 1, 2026, so PT = PDT = UTC-7.
11:59 PM PDT = 06:59 UTC on Oct 31, 2026.

Madrid: CEST ends Oct 25, 2026, so on Oct 31 Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.
06:59 UTC + 1 = 07:59 Madrid time on Oct 31, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Monday is November 2, 2026, 10:00 AM Los Angeles time.

In early November 2026, Los Angeles is still on PDT (DST ends Nov 1, 2026). Wait — DST ends on the first Sunday of November, which is November 1, 2026. So by Monday Nov 2, LA is on PST (UTC-8).

Spain ends DST on the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026), so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by Nov 2.

Difference: UTC+1 - (UTC-8) = 9 hours ahead.

10:00 AM PST = 7:00 PM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2).
Add 48 hours → Monday, October 26, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time.

Note: DST in Spain ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026 at 03:00 (clocks go back to 02:00). Since the question asks for the end time in local (Madrid) time, the wall clock still reads 18:00 on October 26 — but actually, because 48 hours of elapsed real time crosses the DST change, the local wall-clock time will be 17:00, not 18:00.

Let me verify: Start = Oct 24, 18:00 CEST (UTC+2) = Oct 24, 16:00 UTC. Add 48 hours → Oct 26, 16:00 UTC. On Oct 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), so local time = 17:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Start: Oct 26, 2026, 10:00 AM PT (PDT, UTC-7, since DST ends Nov 1, 2026).
End: Oct 29, 2026, 10:00 AM PDT = 17:00 UTC.
Madrid on Oct 29, 2026: CET (UTC+1), since EU DST ends Oct 25, 2026.
17:00 UTC + 1 = 18:00.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Submissions close Oct 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.

On Nov 1, 2026, the US switches from EDT to EST (DST ends at 2:00 AM local on Nov 1). So Oct 31 at 11:59 PM ET = EDT = UTC-4.

Oct 31, 2026 11:59 PM EDT = Nov 1, 2026 03:59 UTC.

Add 36 hours: Nov 2, 2026 15:59 UTC.

Spain: DST ends on last Sunday of October = Oct 25, 2026. So on Nov 2, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

Nov 2, 2026 15:59 UTC = Nov 2, 2026 16:59 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z (UTC).

Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) in winter. However, I need to check if DST is still in effect on October 25, 2026. In the EU, DST ends on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25, 2026, and the clocks change at 01:00 UTC (03:00 CEST → 02:00 CET).

At 02:30 UTC on October 25, 2026, DST has already ended, so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

02:30 UTC + 1 hour = 03:30 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Last Sunday of October 2026 = October 25, 2026.

Deadline: 11:59 PM PT on Oct 25, 2026.

In late October, US is still on PDT (DST ends Nov 1, 2026), so PDT = UTC-7.
Spain: DST ends last Sunday of October, which is Oct 25, 2026. At 3:00 AM CEST, clocks fall back to 2:00 AM CET. So after Oct 25, 2026, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

11:59 PM PDT Oct 25 = 06:59 UTC Oct 26 = 07:59 CET Oct 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

US DST ends on the first Sunday of November 2026 = November 1, 2026.

At that moment, Eastern Time has already switched back to EST (UTC-5) at 2 AM. So 12:00 noon ET = 12:00 EST = 17:00 UTC.

Lima is UTC-5 year-round, so 17:00 UTC = 12:00 local.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is UTC-12. Deadline is Dec 31, 2026 24:00 AoE = Jan 1, 2027 00:00 at UTC-12 = Jan 1, 2027 12:00 UTC.

Tokyo is UTC+9, so that's Jan 1, 2027 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney on October 5, 2026 is in AEDT (UTC+11, since DST starts first Sunday of October = Oct 4, 2026).

5:00 PM AEDT = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

New York on October 5, 2026 is in EDT (UTC-4, DST ends Nov 1, 2026).

06:00 UTC - 4 = 02:00 EDT on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
